title: Hiring manager, new grad software engineer, average answers

questions.text: Walk me through a project from your internship or coursework that best shows what you can do for this role.
Why this role and why this team?
probe_hints: what you know about the team

questions.text: Tell me about a technical decision you made and how you chose between the options.
How do you like to work with a team and a manager?
What is the largest piece of work you have handled so far?
What do you want to learn in your first year?

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Hi Tomas, thanks for joining. I'm Priya, an engineering manager on the services team. This is a thirty minute conversation about your experience and the role.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Hi Priya, thanks for making time. I'm happy to be here.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Did you find the video link easily today?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Yes, no problem. I tested it this morning, and I'm in my apartment so it is quiet.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Good. I'll ask about three or four things you have worked on, then leave time at the end for your questions.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Walk me through a project from your internship or coursework that best shows what you can do for this role.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: My best example is my internship at Brindle Logistics last summer. We built a dashboard for warehouse staff to see late shipments. I wrote the filter and search part in React, and we used an existing API. It went live before I left and the team said people used it daily.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What part did you build yourself, and what did your mentor handle?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I wrote the search box and the date filters myself. I also fixed a bug where the page reloaded every time someone typed. I fixed it by waiting half a second before sending the request. My mentor handled the API and reviewed all my code.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Why this role and why this team?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I like the work your team does. It seems like a great place to learn and I want to grow as an engineer. I also like that the product is used by real people.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What did you see in the team's work that stood out to you?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I read your engineering blog post about moving to smaller services. I did something similar in a class project, where I split one app into two parts. It was hard and I want to learn how a real team does it.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about a technical decision you made and how you chose between the options.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: In my operating systems course, we had to pick between threads and processes for a small web server. I tried both in a quick test. Threads were faster to start, but a crash in one could take down the server. I picked processes for safety, and the server handled 200 requests per second in our test.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Did you talk to your partner before you decided?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Yes, we talked it over. My partner wanted threads because they were simpler, so I showed him my test results. He agreed in the end, and we kept a short note in our repo about why we chose processes.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Thanks. What questions do you have for me?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: What does a typical first month look like for a new engineer on your team?

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: New engineers get a small real project with a mentor in week one. Most ship something in the first six weeks, and they join the on-call rotation after three months.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: That's all the time we have. Thanks Tomas, the recruiter will follow up within a week.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Thank you, Priya. I enjoyed the conversation.

notes: Average for new grad: real examples but shared credit and few numbers. One vague motivation answer is probed.
